correctness.rationale: For ones at a<b<c, directly counted X_011=2a+b-1, X_110=3n-b-2c-4, X_001=C(a,2)+C(b-1,2)+C(c-2,2). These three statistics determine the other five scattered triple multiplicities using the fixed number of zeros and the first two power sums of zeros preceding each one. Equal decks imply (a,b,c) maps to (a+s,b-2s,c+s); equality of X_001 gives s(3s-(b-a-(c-b)))=0, so there is at most one nontrivial partner and it swaps the two inter-one gaps. Orient x>y to count each pair exactly once; admissible starting positions are 0<=a<=n-1-2y-4s, giving max(0,n-2y-4s) pairs. Summing the finite-at-each-coefficient geometric generating functions proves the rational all-length identity, including n<3 and n<7 boundaries. Independently enumerated all length-three decks for all weight-three words at n=3..17, checked every deck class size and exact collision count.

final_claim: For every n, the number D_{3,3}(n) of distinct scattered length-three decks of binary words of length n with exactly three ones has generating function z^3/(1-z)^4 - z^7/((1-z)^2(1-z^2)(1-z^4)). Every deck class has one or two words; all paired classes are characterized by inter-one gap exchange and counted by sum_{s,y>=1} max(0,n-2y-4s). This proves Chrisnata et al. Conjecture 1.
limitations: Fixed Hamming weight three, alphabet binary, exact scattered subsequence length three; no arbitrary-weight or larger k result.
